entrypoints.summary: The public external loadPrecompilePreimagePart(uint256 _partOffset, address _precompile, bytes calldata _input) accepts caller-selected precompile, input, and part offset.

negative_controls: No run-result artifact is supplied to establish an observed execution.
A precompile call that completes successfully should store the correct result fragment rather than error data.
observability.positive_marker: The outer transaction succeeds and preimageParts contains the precompile out-of-gas error in place of a correct fragment; the report identifies possible incorrect FaultDisputeGame outcome.

preconditions: A correct preimage fragment exists for the targeted precompile/input key and part offset.
The caller can arrange a precompile out-of-gas condition while the outer transaction has enough gas to update storage, as described under the 63/64 rule.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Caller-selected address _precompile, bytes _input, uint256 _partOffset, and transaction gas conditions inducing the reported precompile out-of-gas path.
trigger_steps.summary: Invoke the public loader with the selected precompile, input, and target part offset under gas conditions that exhaust the precompile but not the outer call.

capabilities.concept: Induce precompile out-of-gas while retaining outer-call gas

mitigations.concept: Revert instead of storing data after precompile out-of-gas

relation_candidates.dst: Induce precompile out-of-gas while retaining outer-call gas
relation_candidates.rationale: The public entrypoint permits caller-supplied precompile and input, and the report describes a caller providing insufficient gas to cause the precompile out-of-gas condition.
The 63/64 forwarding rule can leave enough gas for the outer function to store the error bytes after precompile out-of-gas, overwriting a successful fragment.
relation_candidates.src: Induce precompile out-of-gas while retaining outer-call gas

relation_candidates.rationale: The report links correct preimageParts required for VM.step reproduction to the possibility of an incorrect FaultDisputeGame outcome when they are overwritten.

relation_candidates.dst: Revert instead of storing data after precompile out-of-gas
relation_candidates.rationale: The recommendation is to revert on precompile out-of-gas rather than update state, preventing error data from replacing a correct fragment.

impact.affected_asset: Correct preimageParts state used to reproduce VM.step in FaultDisputeGame.step.
impact.attacker_capability: Overwrite a correct stored preimage fragment for a caller-selected precompile/input key and offset with an induced out-of-gas error while the outer transaction succeeds.
impact.security_effect: Poisoned preimage-part state can cause an incorrect FaultDisputeGame outcome.

causal_trace.summary: An external caller can repeatedly invoke the public precompile-loading function using chosen precompile address, input, and part offset; the preimageParts key includes the precompile address and input.
A call with the same precompile and input is expected to reproduce the same key and state update, but a precompile revert causes returned error data to be stored in the same preimageParts mapping.

The staticcall forwards gas(), but the 63/64 gas rule can leave the outer function sufficient gas to commit state after the selected precompile exhausts gas; the out-of-gas error can overwrite a successful fragment at the chosen offset while the transaction succeeds.
Because FaultDisputeGame.step requires correct preimageParts to reproduce VM.step, the report states that the poisoned fragment can lead to an incorrect dispute outcome.

failure.operation: Commit of precompile out-of-gas error bytes into preimageParts after staticcall failure

primary_invariant.statement: For a given precompile address, input, and part offset, preimageParts should retain the correct precompile-result fragment needed for VM.step reproduction rather than failure bytes under the successful-result key.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The function catches a reverted precompile invocation and writes its returned error bytes to preimageParts; an attacker can induce an out-of-gas revert yet leave enough outer-call gas for that write.

provenance.source_id: Spearbit Base Fault Proofs no MIPS Security Review, finding 5.1.1

quality.review_notes: The report contains the finding narrative and inline staticcall excerpt, but no standalone source snapshot, remediation commit, or executable test artifact is present in this bundle. It says a related test exists and that Coinbase acknowledged a later fix, but neither a test result nor an implemented fix is evidenced here; reproducibility and remediation status therefore remain unverified.

remediation.invariant_restored: An out-of-gas precompile invocation reverts rather than committing its error data, so failure data cannot replace the valid preimage fragment at the deterministic key and offset.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: A correct fragment for the same precompile/input mapping key and selected offset is present, after which the caller invokes the public loader with gas conditions that make the precompile exhaust gas while the outer function continues.
data_structure_invariants: preimageParts for a deterministic precompile/input key and offset must contain the correct precompile-result fragment.
Failure bytes from a reverted precompile must not be persisted as the result fragment for the same key and offset.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Selects which 32 bytes of the returned result are stored; report states an attacker may overwrite a fragment for some offset.
numeric_domains.name: _partOffset

state_context.state_machine: A public load operation obtains a precompile result and persists a selected 32-byte result part; FaultDisputeGame.step later depends on persisted preimage parts to reproduce VM.step.
